anomalies.observed: On the EthernetAndPower sheet the battery positive terminal U1.1 (+ / MH1) and the barrel-jack switch contact J8.3 are on the same net NET0023, and the battery-feed Schottky U10 (SS2040FL) is connected between NET0023 (its cathode, pin 2) and NET0046 (its anode, pin 1), where NET0046 is the GND-side return of the input capacitor C5. J8.2 is tied to GND, and the in-sheet note states '2 and 3 are shorted with no plug'. Thus, with no DC plug inserted, J8.2–J8.3 are closed and the net that carries the battery + (NET0023) is shorted to GND; the diode never connects the cell to the BAT+ rail that feeds IC2.VIN / USB VBUS / J8.1.
anomalies.expected: The specification requires the battery to be the only source routed through a series diode with 'anode on battery (via U7), cathode on BAT+', and the jack switch contact to sit on the battery return: 'J4.3→BAT-' so that 'the jack's internal switch keeps the battery's return path connected to GND by default, and inserting a DC plug breaks that short — disconnecting the battery.' In other words J8.3 / NET0023 should be the battery NEGATIVE, and U10's cathode should land on BAT+, not on the switch contact.

anomalies.impact: Reintroduces the documented rev-B fault: with no DC adapter plugged in the 18650's positive terminal is shorted to ground through the jack's normally-closed contact, draining/shorting the cell, and the battery cannot power the 3.3 V rail at all (only USB / barrel jack feed BAT+).

parsed.summary: Most of the build matches the spec (FAN53610 topology and values, EPD component set and G1 values, keyboard/SD/UART mapping, and the previously-unconnected RJ45 now wired), but the battery-feed section is mis-wired: the cell's positive terminal is tied to the barrel-jack switch contact (NET0023) and to the diode cathode instead of to BAT+, so the normally-closed pin2–pin3 contact shorts the battery to ground when no plug is inserted — the very 'SHORTS BATTERY' condition the design was supposed to fix.
